questions.prompt: Masses \(2.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) at \(x=0\) and \(6.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) at \(x=4.0\,\mathrm{m}\) lie on a line. Find \(x_{\mathrm{cm}}\).
A system has total momentum \(30\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}\) and total mass \(10\,\mathrm{kg}\). Find the center-of-mass speed.
Three masses lie on the \(x\)-axis: \(1.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) at \(0\), \(2.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) at \(3.0\,\mathrm{m}\), and \(3.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) at \(6.0\,\mathrm{m}\). Find \(x_{\mathrm{cm}}\).
A \(12\,\mathrm{kg}\) system has net external force \(18\,\mathrm{N}\) in the \(+x\)-direction. Find \(a_{\mathrm{cm}}\).
A \(2.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) object has velocity \(4\hat{\imath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), and a \(3.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) object has velocity \(-\hat{\imath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find \(\vec{v}_{\mathrm{cm}}\).
questions.answer:
Total momentum is
\[
\vec{P}=2.0(4\hat{\imath})+3.0(-\hat{\imath})=5\hat{\imath}
\]
Total mass is \(5.0\,\mathrm{kg}\), so
\[
\vec{v}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\hat{\imath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: Two masses \(m\) and \(3m\) are released from rest by an internal spring on a frictionless table. If the lighter mass moves right at speed \(6.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), find the heavier mass velocity.
questions.answer:
Initial total momentum is zero:
\[
m(6.0)+3m v=0
\]
\[
v=-2.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
The heavier mass moves left.

questions.prompt: A \(60\,\mathrm{kg}\) person walks \(3.0\,\mathrm{m}\) forward relative to a \(140\,\mathrm{kg}\) boat. The water exerts negligible horizontal force. How far does the boat move? Interpret the sign.
questions.answer:
Let \(x_b\) be the boat displacement in the person's walking direction. The person moves \(x_b+3.0\) relative to the shore. With no horizontal external impulse,
\[
140x_b+60(x_b+3.0)=0
\]
\[
200x_b=-180
\]
\[
x_b=-0.90\,\mathrm{m}
\]
The negative sign means the boat moves opposite the person's walking direction.

questions.prompt: An isolated two-object system has total mass \(5.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) and center-of-mass velocity \(2\hat{\imath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). One object has mass \(2.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) and velocity \(5\hat{\imath}+\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the other object's velocity.
questions.answer:
The system momentum is
\[
\vec{P}=M\vec{v}_{\mathrm{cm}}=5.0(2\hat{\imath})=10\hat{\imath}
\]
Object 1 has momentum
\[
\vec{p}_1=2.0(5\hat{\imath}+\hat{\jmath})=10\hat{\imath}+2\hat{\jmath}
\]
Thus object 2 has
\[
\vec{p}_2=-2\hat{\jmath}
\]
Its mass is \(3.0\,\mathrm{kg}\), so
\[
\vec{v}_2=-\frac{2}{3}\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: Two spacecraft modules of masses \(m\) and \(2m\) are initially docked and drifting force-free. An internal actuator separates them by distance \(d\) along the \(x\)-axis. Find each module's displacement from the original center of mass. State the assumption and interpret why the center of mass does not move.
questions.answer:
Assume no external force acts during separation, so the original center of mass stays fixed. Let the lighter module be at \(x_1\) and the heavier at \(x_2\):
\[
mx_1+2mx_2=0
\]
and
\[
x_1-x_2=d
\]
Solving gives
\[
x_1=\frac{2d}{3},\qquad x_2=-\frac{d}{3}
\]
Interpretation: internal actuation can change separation, but it cannot move the center of mass of the isolated two-module system.

questions.prompt: A thin rod of length \(L\) lies on the \(x\)-axis from \(0\) to \(L\), with linear density \(\lambda(x)=\lambda_0(1+\alpha x/L)\). Derive \(x_{\mathrm{cm}}\) and state the allowed range of \(\alpha\) for nonnegative density along the rod.
questions.answer:
The total mass is
\[
M=\int_0^L \lambda_0\left(1+\frac{\alpha x}{L}\right)dx
\]
\[
M=\lambda_0L\left(1+\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)
\]
The first moment is
\[
\int_0^L x\lambda(x)\,dx=\lambda_0L^2\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\alpha}{3}\right)
\]
Therefore
\[
x_{\mathrm{cm}}=L\frac{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\alpha}{3}}{1+\frac{\alpha}{2}}
\]
For nonnegative density over the whole rod, require
\[
1+\frac{\alpha x}{L}\ge0\quad\text{for }0\le x\le L
\]
so
\[
\alpha\ge -1
\]
Positive \(\alpha\) shifts the center of mass toward \(x=L\).
